# markdown-s2 — Safe Markdown → HTML renderer (tier S2) ## Module: `src/markdown.js` (ES module) - `export function render(markdown: string, { headingIds = false } = {}): string` → HTML. - `export function toc(markdown: string): Array<{ level: number, text: string, slug: string }>` — every ATX/setext heading in document order; `text` is the heading's plain text (inline markup removed). - `export function slugify(text: string, seen?: Map)` — GitHub-style slug: lower-case; remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`; spaces → `-`. When a `Map` of previously seen slugs is passed, repeated slugs get `-1`, `-2`, … suffixes. `toc` and `headingIds` use one map per document. ## Output conventions Follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) plus GFM tables and strikethrough, except where this spec says otherwise. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags is not significant to the tests; `
`/`
`, `
`/`
`, ``/`` are equivalent; table alignment may be expressed as `align="left"` or `style="text-align:left"`. Required features: - ATX headings `#`…`######` (closing `#`s stripped), setext headings (`===`, `---`). With `headingIds: true`, headings get `id=""`: `

My title

`. - Paragraphs; soft line breaks preserved as `\n`; hard breaks via two trailing spaces or a trailing backslash → `
`. - Emphasis/strong with `*` and `_` (CommonMark rules incl. no intraword `_` emphasis), `***x***` → `x`; GFM `~~strike~~` → ``. - Code spans (multi-backtick delimiters, one leading/trailing space stripped when both present). - Fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~, info string → `class="language-"`) and indented code blocks. - Blockquotes (nested, with lazy continuation lines), thematic breaks (`---`, `***`, `___`). - Bullet lists (`-`, `*`, `+`) and ordered lists (`1.` / `1)`, `start` attribute when not 1), nesting by indentation, tight vs loose lists (`

  • ` when loose). - Inline links `[t](url "title")`, images `![alt](src "title")`, reference links `[t][ref]`, `[ref]` with definitions `[ref]: url "title"` (case-insensitive labels), autolinks `` and `<>` (→ `mailto:`). - Backslash escapes; HTML-escape `& < > "` in text, attributes and code. - GFM pipe tables with header row, delimiter row, optional alignment (`:--`, `:-:`, `--:`), inline markup in cells, `\|` escapes. ## Safety (deliberate deviation from CommonMark) - Raw HTML (block and inline) is NOT passed through: it is rendered as escaped text, e.g. `` → `

    <script>x</script>

    `. - Link/image URLs with schemes `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` (except `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`) are replaced by `#`. ## CLI: `src/cli.js` `node src/cli.js [--toc] [--ids]` prints HTML (or with `--toc`, the TOC as JSON) to stdout. Reads stdin when the file argument is `-`. .: PROVENANCE.json SPEC.md package.json tests ./tests: public ./tests/public: smoke.test.js { "name": "markdown-s2", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "module", "scripts": { "test": "node --test" } } [] import { test } from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { render } from '../../src/markdown.js'; const n = s => s.replace(/\s*(<\/?(?:p|h[1-6]|ul|ol|li|blockquote|pre|table|thead|tbody|tr|th|td|hr)\b[^>]*>)\s*/g, '$1').trim(); test('heading + paragraph', () => { assert.equal(n(render('# Hi\n\nSome *text*.')), '

    Hi

    Some text.

    '); }); test('raw html escaped', () => { assert.equal(n(render('x')), '

    <b>x</b>

    '); });

content.text:
I've built the Markdown-to-HTML renderer described in SPEC.md, and all 9 tests pass under `node --test` (the 2 public smoke tests plus 7 I added in `tests/public/features.test.js`). I wrote all the code myself, so `PROVENANCE.json` stays `[]`, and nothing outside the standard library is used.

**What's in `src/`:**
- **`markdown.js`** provides `render`, `toc` and `slugify`. It follows the same two-stage design as the commonmark.js reference: first it splits the document into blocks, then it parses the inline text inside each block. It covers:
  - ATX and setext headings, with optional `id`s
  - paragraphs, soft line breaks and hard line breaks
  - blockquotes, including nesting and lazy continuation lines
  - bullet and ordered lists, with the `start` attribute and tight vs loose detection
  - fenced and indented code blocks, with tab handling
  - thematic breaks
  - reference link definitions, with case-insensitive labels
  - the CommonMark emphasis rules, plus `~~strikethrough~~`
  - code spans, inline and reference links and images, and autolinks (including `mailto:`)
  - backslash escapes and entities
  - GFM pipe tables, with alignment, inline markup in cells and `\|` escapes
- **Safety:** raw HTML is never output as HTML; it appears as escaped text. Links and images using `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` are replaced with `#`. The one exception is `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`, which is allowed through.
- **`slugify`** produces GitHub-style slugs and adds `-1`, `-2`, … for repeated headings. `toc` and `headingIds` each use one counter per document.
- **`cli.js`** runs as `node src/cli.js <file|-> [--toc] [--ids]`. I tried both a file and piped input.
- **`entities.js`** holds the named character references (`©`, `—` and so on).

**Limitations that could affect the hidden tests:**
- **Partial entity list:** the named-entity table covers about 230 common entities, not the full HTML5 list. Unknown names are shown as literal text, so a rare one like `⅝` won't be decoded.
- **Text inside escaped HTML is still formatted:** Markdown is still applied to the text inside an escaped tag, so `<a title="*x*">` gets emphasis inside the escaped tag text. The spec doesn't settle this. The alternative is to treat each tag as one unformatted piece of text, which is a small change if the tests expect that.
